svg.text: Severe malnutrition: the child is fragile, not merely hungry
Feeding too much, too fast, is a recognised cause of death
Stabilisation — first days
F-75: low energy, low protein, low sodium
Small feeds, every two to three hours,
through the night as well as the day
Keep warm, treat hypoglycaemia, antibiotics
even with no visible sign of infection
No iron yet — it feeds the infection
Rehabilitation — once appetite returns
F-100 or ready-to-use therapeutic food
Larger feeds, less often, for catch-up growth
Iron is added now, not before
Play and stimulation — the brain was starved too
Teach the mother the feed she will make at home
Discharge without this is readmission with extra steps
Refeeding: why fast feeding kills
A starved body has shut down its heart, liver and kidneys to survive on very little
A sudden load of energy pulls potassium, phosphate and magnesium into the cells
The blood levels crash, the heart fails, and the child dies while apparently improving
Dehydration is judged differently
Skin pinch and sunken eyes mislead in a
wasted child — the skin is loose anyway
Use ReSoMal, slowly, and watch for a rising
pulse and breathing rate: that is overload
The sign that outranks the measurements
Pitting oedema of both feet means severe
malnutrition whatever the weight says
The fluid adds weight and hides the wasting,
so a plump-looking child can be the sickest
